newsitem.title: ITALY: Bertinotti says he against delayed Italy EMU entry.
newsitem.headline: Bertinotti says he against delayed Italy EMU entry.

text.p: Fausto Bertinotti, leader of Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation party, said he opposed any idea of a delayed entry of Italy into European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Asked if he agreed with some of the country's business leaders that Italy should be among a second wave of nations to adopt the single currency, Bertinotti told reporters "no, I think we should all join the single currency together."
"The single currency concept should be pursued, but with some flexibility which takes into account the fact that there is a risk of recession," he added.
Bertinotti's party is not a member of Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government but it holds the balance of power in Italy's lower house of parliament.
He said in February that Italy, in accord with other European nations, should work together to achieve a slackening of the strict criteria and calendar set by the Maastricht Treaty for EMU.
Last week, during a visit to London, he said that a single European currency without Italian participation would be impossible to implement.
The third phase of EMU is set to start on January 1, 1999 and the decision about which countries will take part will be taken in spring next year.
